references.text: Reuben had previously tried to save Joseph by suggesting they throw him into the pit instead of killing him, with the plan to bring him back to his father. Therefore, he was so desperate when he discovered that Joseph was gone.
Just as Reuben tore his clothes in grief when he discovered that Joseph was gone, David and his men also tore their clothes when they heard about the deaths of Saul and Jonathan.
Later in the Joseph narrative, the brothers tear their clothes in despair when Joseph's cup is found in Benjamin's sack—a parallel to Reuben's reaction here.
Joshua also tore his clothes and fell to the ground as a sign of grief and despair after the defeat at Ai, an action parallel to Reuben's sorrow.

The act of tearing clothes as a sign of strong reaction is also seen when the high priest tore his clothes during Jesus' trial, although the context there was an accusation of blasphemy rather than grief.
